I am a data scientist in the Office of Economics and Analytics at the FCC. My work focuses on forecasting models, natural language processing, and geospatial analysis for broadband programs.

Before joining the FCC, I worked as a biostatistician in pediatric and gynecologic research. At the Children's Hospital Association, I led the statistical work for several pediatric research groups, analyzing Medicaid claims and national hospital data to study questions ranging from firearm injuries and youth mental health to cystic fibrosis and RSV. I also spent several years collaborating with the Pediatric and Adolescent Gynecology group at the Yale School of Medicine on studies of polycystic ovarian syndrome in adolescents. I received my MS in Biostatistics and BS in Statistics from Florida State University.

Outside of data science, I am interested in hiking, geopolitics, and traveling.

Youth Suicide and Preceding Mental Health Diagnosis

Chaudhary S, Hoffmann JA, Pulcini CD, Zamani M, et al.; CHARGE Collaborative. JAMA Netw Open. 2024;7(7):e2423996. Read the article

A retrospective, cross-sectional analysis of 40,618 youth suicide decedents aged 10 to 24 years in the CDC National Violent Death Reporting System (2010–2021). Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine which sociodemographic characteristics and suicide mechanisms were associated with having a documented mental health diagnosis. Three of five decedents had no documented diagnosis, and odds were lower among racially and ethnically minoritized youth and among firearm suicides.

Conclusions

Three in five of the young people in this study had no documented mental health diagnosis before they died. That gap was widest among racially and ethnically minoritized youths and among those who died by firearm, the most common means of suicide. The findings suggest that prevention can’t wait for a diagnosis. It needs to reach young people more broadly, through fairer access to mental health screening and treatment, counseling for all families on safely storing firearms and other lethal means, and child access protection laws that keep guns out of children’s reach.

Forecasting Traction for New Prediction Markets

Personal project | Python, DuckDB, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost | Polymarket data: 3.8 million markets and 1.27 billion on-chain trades, 2022–2026

  • Gradient boosting
  • Temporal validation
  • Leakage control
  • Calibration under drift
  • Probability forecasting

Summary

Only 56% of new Polymarket markets trade within their first week, and only 37% of sports markets do. This project predicts, at the moment a market is created, the probability that it will trade within 7 days, and ranks new markets by expected dollar volume. Ten model types were compared against two baselines, and on the held-out test period (August–September 2026, 1.5 million markets) the selected LightGBM model reached an AUC of 0.922, against 0.899 for a series-history baseline.

Dataset

  • Markets: 4.05 million binary markets with question text, outcomes, event, dates and resolution.
  • Trades: 1.27 billion on-chain trade fills, November 2022 – October 2026 (about 45 GB), queried with DuckDB.
  • Modeling set: 3.75 million markets created January 2023 – September 2026; 65% sports, 26% crypto.

Objectives

  1. Predict a calibrated 7-day trading probability at creation.
  2. Use only information available at that moment.
  3. Rank new markets by expected dollar volume.

Approach

Target
At least one trade within 7 days of creation, computed from the trade records. The listing's volume field missed 241,000 markets that traded.
Features
Listing structure, event size, and the recent track record of each market's recurring series (196,000 series parsed from slugs), using only outcomes observable at creation. Automated tests confirm no future information leaks in.
Validation
Train through June 2026, validate on July, test on August–September, with 7-day gaps between periods.
Model
Ten model types were trained on the same features and compared on the validation month; LightGBM (200 trees, learning rate 0.05, 31 leaves) was selected. Text features were tested and dropped. Adding trees keeps improving accuracy on held-out markets from the training period but lowers it on the following month at every learning rate tested, so a small model generalizes best under drift (Figure 2).
Calibration
A daily nowcast estimates today's 7-day trading rate from the 24-hour outcomes of markets created 1–8 days earlier and shifts predictions to match, replacing a static recalibration that went stale.
Volume ranking
A separate gradient-boosted regression on log dollar volume ranks new markets by value.

Results

Each model type was tuned on the July 2026 validation month, refit on all markets created before August 1, and scored once on the held-out test period (August 8 – September 27, 2026; 1.5 million markets), with the same daily recalibration applied to every model.

The four gradient-boosted models finished within 0.006 AUC of each other, close to run-to-run noise. LightGBM was best on validation, while CatBoost had the lowest test log loss and XGBoost the highest test AUC. Against the history baseline, the selected model gains most where history is weakest: AUC rises from 0.83 to 0.86 for sports markets and from 0.74 to 0.81 for new series.

The figures below come from the July validation month, where the recalibration and volume-ranking methods were developed with the scikit-learn gradient boosting model.

Conclusion

Whether a new market will trade is largely predictable at creation. Its series’ track record and listing structure carry most of the signal, and on the held-out test period the selected model reached an AUC of 0.92, with the largest gains for sports markets and new series. The choice of algorithm mattered less than expected: the four gradient-boosted models finished almost level, ahead of random forests, logistic regression and a neural network. The harder problem was drift. As automated sports markets flooded the platform, a static recalibration went stale within weeks, while a nowcast built on 24-hour outcomes kept probabilities calibrated without waiting for 7-day labels. And whether a market trades and how much it trades are different questions, so ranking by expected volume is the better tool for prioritizing listings.

Calibration error is expected calibration error. Models were selected on the July 2026 validation month and scored once on the August 8 – September 27, 2026 test period. Personal project, not affiliated with Polymarket.
